name: Torsional Filament Projector TFP-6 'Garrote'
description: The TFP-6 'Garrote' is a compact two-handed projector that launches a dense web of monomolecular torsional filaments across a target corridor or open space, creating an invisible lattice of cutting wire suspended between electromagnetic anchor nodes fired simultaneously from the weapon's twin barrels. The filaments are composed of carbon-ceramic composite strands under extreme torsional tension — wound so tightly during manufacture that contact with any moving mass causes them to snap-cut rather than deflect, delivering kinetic laceration energy far beyond what their apparent mass would suggest. The anchor nodes embed into walls, floors, and structural surfaces on contact, maintaining filament tension for up to ninety seconds before degrading.
specifications:
weight: 4.2 kg (unloaded), 5.9 kg (loaded, dual cassettes)
length: 71 cm
filament range: 3–18 m effective web span
anchor node count: 8 per deployment (4 per barrel)
filament tension duration: 90 seconds nominal, 60 seconds under load
cassette capacity: 1 deployment per cassette
reload time: ~45 seconds (manual cassette replacement)
filament visibility: Invisible to naked eye; detectable by Tier 2+ optical enhancement
effective environments: Enclosed spaces, corridors, vehicle interiors, stairwells
contraindications: Open spaces with wind above 15 kph (filament drift degrades lattice integrity)
tactical_use: The 'Garrote' is a pure area-denial and ambush weapon. Standard doctrine calls for deployment in advance of expected enemy movement — operators establish a filament web across a chokepoint, then trigger pursuit or drive targets into the kill zone. In close-quarters building clearance, teams use the 'Garrote' to seal off retreat routes or cut off reinforcements from a target room. Some operators deploy webs at ankle and throat height simultaneously, using staggered cassettes to create multi-level lattices. Counter-filament protocols exist but require specialized equipment most street-level operators don't carry.
cultural_context: The 'Garrote' carries a particular stigma even among GLMZ's mercenary community, where most weapons are accepted as tools of the trade. The nature of filament injuries — clean, almost surgical cuts that can remove fingers, hands, or worse depending on velocity of contact — has given the weapon an association with cruelty that purely kinetic weapons don't carry. Corporate security firms that deploy it publicly face significant reputational risk, so its use is largely deniable and off-the-books. Among Arcturus Defense Solutions' contractor network, 'Garrote' operators are known as 'lacemakers' — a term that carries both professional respect and quiet unease.
known_users: Arcturus Defense Solutions black operations contractors
Corporate extraction teams operating in restricted infrastructure
Ringo Corponation facility hardening crews (off-label use)
story_hooks: A corporate executive was found dead in a sealed boardroom — the door was locked from inside and every exit was covered in a degraded filament web. The question isn't how the killer got in. It's how they got out.

An Arcturus Defense Solutions shipment of 'Garrote' cassettes has been intercepted and repurposed by a gang controlling the Undertow sewer network — they've been using them to create impassable zones that are slowly starving out competing factions.

A player character's contact has gone silent in a district where someone has been deploying 'Garrote' webs indiscriminately in civilian corridors. The local medical bay is overwhelmed with laceration cases.
Arcturus is quietly offering a bounty for the return of a prototype 'Garrote' variant that fires self-repairing filaments — the kind that don't degrade after ninety seconds.
related_entities: Carrion Defense Works Autonomous Perimeter Defense Ecosystem

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, angular two-handed projector with a distinctly predatory silhouette. Twin parallel barrels angle slightly downward from a reinforced central spine, giving it the asymmetrical posture of something coiled and ready to strike. The weapon has an almost skeletal aesthetic — all structural necessity, no ornamentation.
physical_description.dimensions: 71 cm length overall; 34 cm grip-to-rear-sight span; twin barrels separated 8 cm center-to-center; approximately 18 cm depth at the cassette housing
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty but well-balanced across the two-hand grip. The 5.9 kg loaded weight feels distributed toward the barrel assemblies, creating a slight forward-heavy sensation that rewards aggressive two-handed control. Unloaded (4.2 kg) it feels almost delicate by comparison, deceptively light for its lethality.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer chassis (titanium-carbon composite in military-spec models) with steel barrel sleeves and electromagnetic anchor emitters. The cassette housing is tool-steel with brushed finish.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with brushed steel barrel sleeves showing micro-etching from manufacturing. Military contractor versions feature light battle-wear — scuffed edges, faint stress marks around the cassette release, occasional tool-mark scratches suggesting field maintenance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body with darker charcoal polymer grip sections. Subtle teal accent striping (ARCTURUS DEFENSE house color) along the upper receiver and cassette release lever. Steel anchor emitter tips show dull metallic shine.
physical_description.grip_texture: Dual ergonomic grip zones with cross-hatched rubberized polymer designed for both bare-hand and gloved operation. The rear grip slightly narrower than the forward grip, encouraging a natural two-handed weapon mount. Palm swell prominent to reduce recoil stress from electromagnetic discharge.
distinctive_features: Twin parallel barrels with visible aperture tuning rings etched in 1mm increments
Electromagnetic emitter nodes recessed into barrel ends — faint blue-green LED indicators pulse during charge cycle
Dual cassette housing with bayonet-lock mechanism and witness holes showing filament spool status
Upper-receiver-mounted targeting reference laser (Class 3, visible only under low-light conditions)
Vent ports along barrel sleeves allowing electromagnetic discharge cooling
Recessed maintenance access panel with hex-socket fasteners
Safety lever integrated into trigger guard with three-position detent: SAFE, ARMED, DEPLOY
Faint serial plate on the lower receiver with ARCTURUS DEFENSE logo and military spec designation
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS logo (stylized compass rose) embossed on the upper rear receiver. Serial plate mounted on lower left side reads 'TFP-6/GAR-7' with batch designation and production date. Small restrictive-use warning stamp on both cassette housings. Contractor marks and field modifications common on veteran units.
physical_description.condition_typical: Military examples show field-worn aesthetic: scuffed polymer, faded accent striping, residual scoring on barrel sleeves from equipment contact. Electronics fully functional but cosmetic wear evident. Well-maintained contractor units show evidence of regular cleaning and calibration. No cosmetic rust (electronics-sealed construction), but polymer degradation visible near grip zones from operator perspiration and handling.
